title: Fertilizer in Tagalog: Abono, Pataba and the Words Farmers Use
metaTitle: Fertilizer in Tagalog: Abono, Pataba and More
metaDescription: Fertilizer in Tagalog is abono or pataba. Learn the Tagalog words for organic and chemical fertilizer, urea, applying fertilizer, and what farmers say.
excerpt: The usual word for fertilizer in Tagalog is abono. Farmers also say pataba, from the root taba, which means fat or rich, because fertilizer makes the soil rich. In the field you will hear both, often mixed with English names like urea, complete and potash. This guide lists the Tagalog fertilizer words farmers really use, with what each one means.

blocks.text:
Ask a farmer in Nueva Ecija about fertilizing and you may hear, "Mag aabono ako sa Lunes." Ask what they will use and they will likely name it in English: urea, complete or ammosul. That mix of Tagalog and English is how fertilizer is really talked about on Filipino farms.

So this guide gives you both: the Tagalog words, and the English names that farmers use beside them. For more farm words, see our guide to [farm words in Tagalog](/blog/farm-words-in-tagalog).
Fertilizer in Tagalog: abono and pataba

**Abono** comes from the Spanish word for fertilizer, and it is the word most farmers use for any fertilizer, especially the kind sold in sacks. **Pataba** comes from taba, so it means something that makes the soil rich. Many people use pataba most for natural fertilizer like manure and compost, but it can mean any fertilizer.

The verbs follow the nouns. You will hear mag abono, to fertilize, and nag abono, fertilized. Paglalagay ng abono means applying fertilizer.

The same root taba gives other farm words. **Matabang lupa** means fertile soil, dark and rich. **Patabain ang lupa** means to make the soil rich, which is the whole reason for adding abono or compost. And when a crop turns lush and dark green after fertilizing, farmers often call it mataba, the same word used for a well fed animal.

blocks.text: Most sack fertilizers keep their English or trade names, even in a Tagalog sentence. That is why it helps to know what each name means.

items: **Urea:** the white nitrogen fertilizer, 46 0 0. See [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer).
**Complete:** 14 14 14, with equal nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. See [complete fertilizer 14 14 14](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14).
**Ammophos or 16 20 0:** a phosphorus rich basal fertilizer. See [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer).
**Potash or 0 0 60:** muriate of potash. See [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer).
**Foliar:** liquid fertilizer sprayed on the leaves. See [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer).

blocks.text: Each answer has its own guide: [bags of fertilizer per hectare](/blog/bags-of-fertilizer-per-hectare), [fertilizer timing by growth stage](/blog/fertilizer-timing-by-growth-stage), [yellow rice leaves](/blog/yellow-rice-leaves) and [fertilizer price in the Philippines](/blog/fertilizer-price-philippines).

Fertilizer and weeds go together, because weeds steal the abono you put down. In Tagalog, both weeds and grass are called **damo**. Farmers name each weed by its own local name too, like bayakibok for barnyard grass, mutha for purple nutsedge and makahiya for the sensitive plant. Our guide on [common weeds in the Philippines](/weeds/common-weeds-philippines) lists them with photos.

blocks.title: Say it the way you know it
blocks.text: You do not need perfect English to get good fertilizer advice. Ask in Tagalog, Taglish or English, using the words you already use in the field.

Anee, the smart farm technician in anee.io, answers in Tagalog or English, the way you ask. Ask "Kailan ako mag aabono?" and Anee reads your lot's planting day, crop stage and weather before answering. The [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) then puts each fertilizer application on its date. Read more about our [Tagalog farm app](/blog/tagalog-farm-app).

items.a: Abono is the everyday word. Pataba is also used, often for natural fertilizer like manure and compost.

items.q: What is organic fertilizer in Tagalog?
items.a: Organikong abono, or simply pataba. It covers compost, manure and vermicast.

items.q: How do you say apply fertilizer in Tagalog?
items.a: Mag abono, or maglagay ng abono. Paglalagay ng abono means the act of applying fertilizer.
Farmers just say urea. It is the white nitrogen fertilizer with the grade 46 0 0.

items.q: Where does the word abono come from?
items.a: From Spanish, where abono also means fertilizer. It entered Tagalog during the Spanish period.
